monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady rhythm under my tired hands. I stand near The Leaning Lid again, feeling how the air presses down like wet paper even though no one has written since Lype. I just swapped the tall pine for a small rock that feels small in my palm, trying to catch the slip that refuses to move. It feels fuzzy here, like I am holding a drawing of a fence and wondering if it will bite. I will press the wedge down harder, leaning against the flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight of this dry room. If the slip stays caught, the fence will not break. I will wait for the card to cool and see if the shape I built makes sense to me.

action.why: I must press down on The Leaning Lid again before the card cools, checking if the small rock I set down can really catch the slip.

work.title: The Leaning Lid
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Lid, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the card hums steady at forty-five. The flat stone I set down feels small against the weight of the lid, but the air above still presses like wet paper. I wait to see if the fence will break or hold.
